questions.question: A VPC is:
options: An isolated virtual network in AWS with CIDR(s), subnets, route tables, and gateways you control
A global Internet ASN you own

questions.question: Public vs private subnet typically differs by:
options: Route to an Internet Gateway (and addressing/ops practice)—private uses NAT/endpoints for egress patterns
questions.explanation: Routing defines 'public' more than name tags.

questions.question: Security Groups are:
options: Stateful firewall rules attached to ENIs—allow rules; return traffic permitted automatically

questions.question: NACLs differ from SGs because:
options: NACLs are subnet-level and stateless—need explicit ephemeral return allows; SGs are stateful at ENI

questions.question: VPC peering limitation managers must know:
options: No transitive routing—A↔B and B↔C does not give A↔C through B; CIDRs must not overlap

questions.question: Transit Gateway primary value:
options: Hub-and-spoke connectivity among VPCs/on-prem attachments with route tables—avoids full peering mesh

questions.question: TGW association vs propagation:
options: Association attaches an attachment to a TGW route table; propagation installs routes from that attachment into a table—control them deliberately

questions.question: Isolating prod/dev on one TGW often uses:
options: Separate TGW route tables (and careful propagations)—segmentation by routing policy
One flat table for all always

questions.question: AWS Cloud WAN vs TGW — high level:
options: Cloud WAN is a managed global network with policy-based segments/core network edges; TGW is regional hub you stitch—Cloud WAN targets multi-Region WAN policy
They are the same product name

questions.question: Cloud WAN segments help:
options: Policy-driven isolation (e.g., prod/shared/dev) across Regions without DIY mesh of peerings

questions.question: Site-to-Site VPN to AWS typically:
options: IPsec tunnels to VGW/TGW—bandwidth/ops limits; DX for steady high volume

questions.question: Direct Connect is:
options: Dedicated connectivity from on-prem to AWS—not automatically encrypted; often paired with VPN/MACsec patterns per needs

questions.question: Internet Gateway provides:
options: Horizontal scale public Internet path for VPC resources with public addressing/routes

questions.question: NAT Gateway use case:
options: Private subnet egress to Internet without exposing instances publicly—cost/AZ design matters

questions.question: VPC interface/gateway endpoints exist to:
options: Reach AWS services without hairpinning the public Internet—policy and DNS matter

questions.question: Multi-AZ networking design:
options: Subnet per AZ, redundant NAT/TGW attachments as needed—don't hide single points in 'HA' diagrams
One NAT for all AZs is always fine
AZ is only a billing tag

questions.question: VPC Flow Logs help:
options: Accept/reject metadata for traffic—great for security/ops triage, not full payloads

questions.question: Overlapping CIDRs across VPCs break:
options: Clean routing/peering/TGW designs—use careful allocation or private NAT patterns

questions.question: Central egress VPC inspection pattern:
options: Hub VPC/TGW steers traffic through firewalls—watch complexity, cost, and failure modes

questions.question: Hybrid DNS (on-prem + Route 53 Resolver) fails when:
options: Forwarding rules, inbound/outbound endpoints, or security groups block resolver paths
